# Jubilees Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Covenant of the Pieces; God's Promise; Hagar

---

**14:1** After all this, in the fourth year of the week, on the first day of the third month, the LORD's word came to Abram in a dream: "Don't be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your immeasurably great reward."

**14:2** Abram said: "LORD, what can you give me? I have no child. The son of my maidservant Masek — Eliezer from Damascus — he's the one who'll inherit everything. You haven't given me any descendants of my own."

**14:3** The voice said: "No — that man will not be your heir. The one who comes from your own body will inherit."

**14:4** God brought Abram outside and said: "Look up at the sky. Try to count the stars if you can."

**14:5** Abram looked up and saw the stars spreading out beyond counting. And the word came: "That is what your descendants will be like."

**14:6** Abram believed God. And God counted that trust as righteousness.

**14:7** God said: "I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees to give you this land."

**14:8** Abram said: "LORD God, how will I actually know that I'm going to inherit it?"

**14:9** God said: "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old she-goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."

**14:10** Abram gathered all of these in the middle of the month and settled near the oak of Mamre by Hebron.

**14:11** He built an altar and sacrificed each animal, poured the blood on the altar, and cut the bodies in half, arranging the pieces opposite each other. But the birds he left whole.

**14:12** Birds of prey swooped down on the carcasses, but Abram kept driving them off and wouldn't let a single bird touch the offering.

**14:13** As the sun began to set, a deep sleep crashed over Abram — and with it came a terrifying, smothering darkness.

**14:14** A voice said: "This is the truth, Abram: your descendants will be strangers in a foreign land. They will be enslaved. They will suffer for four hundred years."

**14:15** "But I will judge the nation that enslaves them, and when it's over your people will come out with great wealth."

**14:16** "You yourself will die in peace, joining your ancestors at a good old age."

**14:17** "Four generations from now, your descendants will come back to this land — because the wickedness of the Amorites hasn't run its full course yet."

**14:18** Abram woke up. He stood and looked: the sun was down, and before him was a smoking furnace and a blazing torch moving between the divided pieces.

**14:19** That day the LORD made a covenant with Abram: "I am giving your descendants this land — from the river of Egypt to the great Euphrates — the territory of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim, the Phiblites, the Hivites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."

**14:20** As the day closed, Abram made the complete offering — the pieces and the birds with grain offerings and drink offerings — and the fire consumed everything.

**14:21** That same day we angels made our covenant with Abram, just as we had covenanted with Noah in this same month. And Abram renewed the festival and its ordinance as his permanent practice.

**14:22** Abram was overjoyed and told Sarai everything. He believed children were coming — but Sarai still wasn't pregnant.

**14:23** Sarai approached her husband with a proposal: "Go to my Egyptian maid Hagar. Maybe through her I can have children." Abram listened and said: "Do what you think is best."

**14:24** Sarai took Hagar her maid and gave her to Abram as an additional wife. Abram went in to Hagar.

---
*PNEUMA notes: "A terrifying, smothering darkness" renders the Ge'ez equivalent of Genesis' "horror of great darkness" vividly. The third-month covenant (v.21) ties this to the Feast of Weeks covenant-renewal theme. "We angels made our covenant" (v.21) — the angelic narrator's first-person confirms angelic participation in the covenant.*
